text:
Marathon Petroleum climbed 3% today, capping a two-week rally of nearly 14%. The main driver appears to be oil price relief: U.S. crude fell today as the Trump administration suspended new duties on Russian goods and signaled sanctions relief, which raised hopes of increased global oil supply and eased earlier geopolitical anxiety. This reversal matters because refiners like Marathon profit when crude prices stabilize or fall relative to what they can sell refined products for — lower input costs improve margins.

The broader backdrop supports this move. Over the past week, oil had spiked sharply on Iran's Hormuz strait attacks and escalating tensions, but today's diplomatic signal suggesting de-escalation has unwound those fears. Refineries are running at a healthy 93.5% capacity, positioned to capture gains if crude stays moderately priced and margins improve from the supply outlook shift.
